reason: The WebXR half of the claim is confirmed exactly by the cited source and by independent sources. caniuse.com/webxr (opened) lists Safari on iOS "3.2 - 26.6: Not supported", "27.0: Not supported", "27.1 - 27.2: Not supported", so "through version 27.2" is the precise current figure (desktop Safari is "Disabled by default" from 13 through 27.1/TP, also not usable). MDN browser-compat-data api/XRSystem.json (opened raw) has safari version_added false, safari_ios "mirror" (i.e. not supported), and chrome 79 with chrome_android mirroring, confirming the Android/Chrome side. WebKit's Safari 18 beta post (opened) announces WebXR only for "Safari 18 for visionOS 2", not iOS. The AR Quick Look half is also confirmed: WebKit blog 8421 (opened) documents `<a rel="ar" href="model.usdz">` with the USDZ format on Safari for iOS 12+, and Apple's Quick Look gallery page (opened) says Quick Look displays USDZ files on iPhone and iPad, requiring iOS 12 or later. The one inaccuracy is the sweeping clause "any in-browser AR overlay is Android-only": that is overbroad. Camera-based WebAR engines that do not use WebXR (getUserMedia + WebGL + device motion) do run in iOS Safari. Zappar's Universal AR compatibility page (opened) lists "Safari for iOS (version 11.3 and later)" in its top "Best" tier, and AR.js docs (opened) state it "works on any phone with webgl and webrtc" without mentioning WebXR and note iOS Safari fixes in LocAR.js. So the claim is directionally right (WebXR is absent on iOS Safari through 27.2; AR Quick Look with USDZ is Apple's native path), but the "any in-browser AR overlay" scope should be narrowed to WebXR-based overlays. Note: web search budget was exhausted this turn, so verification relied on direct fetches of the cited page and known independent URLs.
corrected_claim: Safari on iOS has no WebXR Device API support in any version listed through 27.2 (caniuse: "27.1 - 27.2: Not supported"; desktop Safari is "Disabled by default"; WebKit ships WebXR only on visionOS Safari). WebXR-based in-browser AR therefore runs only on Android (Chrome 79+ and Chromium-based Android browsers), not on iPhone. Non-WebXR camera-based WebAR (e.g. Zappar, AR.js, 8th Wall, using getUserMedia and WebGL) does still work in iOS Safari 11.3+, so "any in-browser AR overlay is Android-only" is too strong. For Apple's native AR path on iPhone, use AR Quick Look via <a rel="ar" href="model.usdz"> with a USDZ file (Safari on iOS 12+). Sources: https://caniuse.com/webxr ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/main/api/XRSystem.json ; https://webkit.org/blog/15443/news-from-wwdc24-webkit-in-safari-18-beta/ ; https://webkit.org/blog/8421/viewing-augmented-reality-assets-in-safari-for-ios/ ; https://developer.apple.com/augmented-reality/quick-look/ ; https://docs.zap.works/universal-ar/javascript/getting-started/compatibility/ ; https://ar-js-org.github.io/AR.js-Docs/
